shadow:
Life cannot be held in place. A car turns a corner it should not have turned. A diagnosis arrives on a Tuesday. The street that was bombed and the street that was not were two doors apart, and no one chose which. Some part of the body has always known this, and it never fully relaxes.

That low hum is agitation. It is the body braced against a blow it cannot see coming, so it stays half ready all the time. The jaw does not unclench. Sleep stays thin. The mind jumps from one thing to the next as if speed could keep it ahead of the shock. It also feeds the urge to be first, to climb over others, because being on top feels for a moment like being safe.

Most people read this as a flaw in their wiring and try to drill it out with more discipline. That tightens the grip. The energy itself is not the problem. Agitation is a portal standing open with nothing pointed through it. The restlessness is not asking to be silenced. It is asking to be aimed at something, and that is slower work than it sounds.
repressive: Some people meet the agitation by quietly giving up. The hope leaks out, the days flatten, and they call this their nature. The fear of facing the fear keeps them from the one move that would free them.
reactive: Others throw the charge outward. They pick fights, take wild risks, court danger close enough to feel it. The hostility looks like nerve. Underneath it is the same fear, just turned up loud enough to drown.
gift:
Something shifts when a person stops trying to flatten the restlessness and instead leans toward it. Walks straight at the thing that makes the skin crawl. The charge that felt like a threat turns out to be fuel, and it has been waiting for somewhere to go.

That is initiative. It is the willingness to make the first move with no map and no one ahead of you on the trail. It means closing the books, even the good ones, even the teachers you trust, and finding out what your own feet want to do. The path is yours because no one has walked it.

This is a fight, but not the shoving kind. You stop competing with the people around you and start measuring against your own edge. Their work becomes a mirror, not a wall to climb over. And the way through agitation is not force. It is softness. You meet a problem the way a body in tai chi meets a thrust, leaning into it rather than bracing, letting it carry you somewhere you could not have planned. Each time you begin like this, without clutching the result, the beginning changes you back.
siddhi:
Far enough in, the bracing stops. The body that spent its life half ready for the blow finally lets the blow be part of the weather. Shocks still come. They just stop landing as shocks, because there is no separate self standing in one spot for them to hit.

This is awakening, and it does not arrive as a reward for effort. No practice earns it. It comes the way thunder comes, all at once, unasked, and once it has come it does not leave. The one who used to scramble to be first is simply not there, and what flows through the empty space is giving, plain and constant, with nothing in the way of it.

From here the whole road reads differently. The agitation at the start, the jumpiness, the long unease, was never a malfunction. It was the open portal. It was the enormous charge that the rest of this was always going to need, just early, and pointed at nothing yet.
